_comment2: Values here are the EoN defaults (100% frequency etc.) plus the EoN property/territory machinery. Two uses:
_comment3: 1) NEW maps: pass via --map-gen-settings at create time. The engine merges
_comment4: autoplace_settings/entity on top of the planet prototype (which the mod
_comment5: already registers in data), so the entity block below is documentation
_comment6: of what a correct surface carries - harmless to include.
_comment6b: GOTCHA: autoplace_controls is NOT enough. Controls only tune slider
_comment6c: values; an entity autoplaces on a surface only if its name sits in
_comment6d: autoplace_settings.entity.settings (baked at surface creation from the
_comment6e: planet prototype, never re-synced). The LDW save lacked 'scrap' there
_comment6f: because it was created while eon-holmium-ore=true (scrap unregistered,
_comment6g: holmium-ore registered). Keep BOTH registered on a healed save: the
_comment6h: stale holmium-ore entry is inert while holmium is off, and re-activates
_comment6i: if holmium is ever switched back on.
_comment7: 2) EXISTING saves (continuous server maps): the surface's map_gen_settings
_comment8: were baked at creation and only mgs.seed changes survive a scenario
_comment9: reset. If the save was created while startup setting eon-holmium-ore
_comment10: was true, the surface's autoplace_settings.entity.settings contains
_comment11: 'holmium-ore' but NOT 'scrap', so scrap never autoplaces on that
_comment12: surface no matter the mod version (verified live: entity_scrap=false,
_comment13: scrap count 0). To heal such a save, apply the relevant keys to the
_comment14: surface at runtime (scenario reset or console) and regenerate chunks:
_comment19: Then /reset or chunk generation uses the current mod prototypes.

settings._comment: EoN-added entities. Fresh maps get these from the planet prototype in data phase; listing them here documents the registrations an existing surface must carry.
